prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1278; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact at an intersection. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by a lawyer. The driver is named on the policy and the claimant was in the vehicle, as confirmed by the police report and witness statements.

Entry 2: Reviewed the injury against the crash mechanics. The reported shoulder injury matches the kind and force of a side impact of this type well.

Entry 3: Requested medical records. They show long-standing treatment for the same shoulder condition before the crash, and most of the current complaints appear to stem from that earlier condition.

Entry 4: Checked for independent confirmation of the accident. No witnesses, photos or other reports have surfaced beyond the claimant's own account, so the collision itself rests on the claimant's statement alone.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant. The account has remained consistent throughout, and the small details added later did not change the core story. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 6: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. It is still unclear whether all of the claimed damage came from this impact or in part from the prior condition, so the apportionment remains open.

Entry 7: Next steps are a request for prior treatment records and an independent medical review to address how much of the current injury is attributable to this collision.
